sites.name: Greater Boston
sites.sampleNote: Combined across venues (Acton, Commons, Zoo, BC, and related sites)
sites.blurb: Preschool, museum, and campus venues across Greater Boston where children completed trust, forgiveness, inequity, and cooperation games with Boston-area collaborators.

sites.name: New Haven
sites.blurb: Urban U.S. comparison samples for risk, time preference, and subjective social status tasks collected with children in the New Haven area.

sites.name: Durham
sites.blurb: Home of the Mind & Culture Lab. Two- and three-year-olds coordinated keys on the square box apparatus in dyads and triads at the lab and nearby schools.

sites.name: USA (urban)
sites.blurb: Urban U.S. children and adolescents in the epistemic-versus-physical uncertainty dice task. Exact city is not named in the open dataset.

sites.name: Antigonish / StFX
sites.blurb: Canadian children tested near St. Francis Xavier University and surrounding communities on cooperation and inequity-aversion batteries.

sites.name: Vadodara
sites.sampleNote: Primary samples; India also includes separate 1-week and 1-year ladder retest cohorts
sites.blurb: Urban Indian children who completed risk/time preference choices and MacArthur Ladder subjective social status ratings, with follow-up retest waves.

sites.name: Srikakulam
sites.blurb: Children in coastal Andhra Pradesh who played the Inequity Game while reaction times fed drift-diffusion models of fairness.

sites.name: Iran (urban)
sites.blurb: Urban Iranian children and adolescents who chose between Roll-Then-Guess (epistemic) and Guess-Then-Roll (physical) uncertainty games.

sites.name: Tsimané
sites.blurb: Tsimané communities in the Bolivian Amazon—one of three cultures in the epistemic-versus-physical uncertainty study, with minimal prior dice exposure.

sites.name: Mayangna
sites.sampleNote: Supplement cohort in OSF files; not in the main explorer N = 210
sites.blurb: Mayangna communities in Nicaragua who completed a supplementary dice-task cohort alongside the main three-culture sample.

sites.name: Shuar — Upano Valley
sites.blurb: Shuar communities in the Upano Valley who took part in cooperation, risk/time preference, and subjective social status studies.

sites.name: Shuar — Cross-Cutucú
sites.blurb: More remote Cross-Cutucú Shuar communities—key market-integration contrasts for risk, time preference, and ladder status ratings.

sites.name: San Pedro de Saño
sites.blurb: Children in San Pedro de Saño who completed the four-task cooperation battery and the Inequity Game reaction-time protocol.

sites.name: Toba/Qom
sites.blurb: Toba/Qom communities in Argentina’s Gran Chaco who completed risk and time preference choices and MacArthur Ladder ratings.

sites.name: Maya communities
sites.blurb: Maya children in Mexico who played the Inequity Game as part of the seven-society computational fairness study.

sites.name: Tooro / Kasiisi
sites.blurb: Children near Fort Portal and Kasiisi who completed cooperation and inequity tasks across several village schools.

sites.name: Senegal (Dakar area)
sites.blurb: Children in Yoff, Boune, and Diacksao who contributed Inequity Game reaction-time data in the seven-society sample.
